newsitem.title: UK: EMI seen opening higher after results.
newsitem.headline: EMI seen opening higher after results.

text.p: Shares in newly demerged record company EMI Group Plc were seen opening higher on Tuesday after the company reported first half pretax profits in line with expectations and said prospects for the industry looked good.
The shares were indicated 4p firmer at 12.75 stg by 0801 GMT in pre-market trade.
EMI posted pretax profits excluding exceptional items of 112.5 million stg, up 9.4 percent and an interim dividend of 8p per share.
Analysts had been expecting profits of between 90-120 million stg.
"The biggest single improvement to pretax was thanks to the lower interest charge," said SocGen analyst, Jason Crisp.

"Turnover was only up two percent and we saw a fall in sales in North America and Asia Pacific," he said. "What has saved the day has been the buoyancy of the UK market, with sales up 20 percent thanks to a strong market and good market share."
EMI said the results had been achieved against variable growth and mixed results from competitors and added that the prospects for the global music market remained positive.
"The music industry is still reasonably strong but we're at the low point of growth at the moment," Crisp said. "You have to be a bit cautious."

The company said that this year's release schedule was more weighted towards the fourth quarter this year, rather than the third or Christmas quarter like last year. Crisp said it was unlikely that he would be revising his year-end forecasts.
